events.title: Lehman Brothers files for bankruptcy
events.text: The largest bankruptcy in US history froze funding between banks. In October the S&P 500 lost a quarter of its value in ten trading days.

events.title: The VIX closes at its crisis high
events.text: Forced selling by funds and banks took the S&P 500 to its lowest close since 1997.

events.title: The low of the financial crisis
events.text: The S&P 500 closed at its lowest point of the crisis. Volatility stayed high for months before it faded.

events.title: The flash crash
events.text: In the middle of the Greek debt crisis, US indices fell roughly 9% within minutes in the afternoon and recovered most of it, as buy orders vanished from order books.

events.title: First session after the US credit downgrade
events.text: Standard & Poor's cut the US rating from AAA on the Friday evening, in the middle of the euro-area debt crisis.

events.title: "Whatever it takes"
events.text: European Central Bank President Mario Draghi pledged to do whatever it takes to preserve the euro. A calming event: stress in the euro area eased afterwards.

events.title: China devaluation selloff
events.text: Two weeks after China devalued the yuan, world markets gapped lower at the open and the VIX briefly traded above 50.

events.title: Brexit referendum result
events.text: The United Kingdom voted to leave the European Union, against what markets expected. The pound fell to its lowest level in thirty years.

events.title: Brazil: leaked presidential recording
events.text: A recording implicating President Michel Temer became public the evening before. Trading in São Paulo was halted by a circuit breaker.

events.title: The volatility shock
events.text: The VIX more than doubled in one session, and exchange-traded products that were short volatility lost almost all of their value.

events.title: Brazil: truckers' strike
events.text: A nationwide truckers' strike that began on 21 May stopped fuel and food deliveries, months before a presidential election.

events.title: Christmas Eve low
events.text: The end of a three-month fall driven by rising US interest rates and trade tensions.

events.title: COVID-19 reaches Europe
events.text: Lockdowns in northern Italy showed the virus had spread beyond Asia. The fall from the record high of 19 February accelerated.

events.title: The worst day since 1987
events.text: After an emergency Federal Reserve rate cut to zero on the Sunday, US shares fell 12% and trading was halted at the open.

events.title: The COVID low
events.text: The Federal Reserve announced open-ended asset purchases. Shares reached their low that day.

events.title: Inflation shock confirms the bear market
events.text: US inflation of 8.6%, reported on the Friday, led markets to price much faster rate rises. The S&P 500 closed more than 20% below its high.

events.title: Hotter inflation report
events.text: US inflation for August came in above forecasts: the largest one-day fall of the 2022 bear market.

events.title: Silicon Valley Bank fails
events.text: The second-largest US bank failure up to that date, after a run on deposits. The stress stayed mostly inside regional banks.

events.title: Yen carry trade unwind
events.text: After a Bank of Japan rate rise and a weak US jobs report, Japanese shares fell 12% in a day and the VIX briefly traded above 60.

events.title: US tariff announcement
events.text: Broad US import tariffs announced on 2 April, and China's retaliation, produced the largest two-day fall since March 2020.

events.title: Tariff pause
events.text: A 90-day pause on most of the new tariffs produced one of the largest one-day gains on record. Violent rebounds belong to stress periods too.

events.title: AI selloff: sharpest day
events.text: The largest one-day fall so far in the 2026 selloff in technology and AI-related shares.
